definition: Assessing not only an agent's final output, but the exact sequence of intermediate tool calls, arguments, retries, and state transitions.
why_it_matters: Agents can arrive at lucky right answers via dangerous or broken tool paths unless step trajectories are inspected.
how_it_works: Eval runners log emitted tool trajectories and compare them against expected reference sequences, invariant rules, or latency budgets.
common_mistakes: Using overly strict exact sequence ordering checks when equivalent parallel or reordered read calls remain valid.
example: Verifying a support agent queried policy rules before emitting an approved credit adjustment.

definition: Evaluating agent robustness inside reproducible containerized sandboxes, mock enterprise APIs, or simulated user personas.
why_it_matters: Realistic simulated sandboxes catch destructive actions safely before agents touch production accounts or customers.
how_it_works: Harnesses such as WebArena, OSWorld, and tau-bench spin up clean stateful environments, score end database/file states, and reset deterministically.
common_mistakes: Testing agents solely on static text datasets without stateful API side-effect verification.
example: Running customer-policy adherence tests against a simulated airline reservation database and simulated user agent.

definition: Having multiple independent model instances critique, challenge, and refine competing hypotheses before converging on a consensus output.
why_it_matters: Structured peer disagreement lowers overconfident blind spots on complex reasoning and factuality tasks.
how_it_works: Proposer agents generate answers and rationales, inspect peer critiques across rounds, and synthesize revised consensus answers.
common_mistakes: Letting unanimous shared model biases reinforce errors cleanly across homogeneous ungrounded instances.
example: Checking clinical summary accuracy using opposing critic agents verifying claims against source notes.

definition: Security threat where stored dense text embeddings can be inverted back into sensitive source phrasing by adversarial decoders.
why_it_matters: Organizing teams frequently store embeddings with weaker access controls than raw text, creating unexpected confidential leakage.
how_it_works: Inversion models iteratively reconstruct approximate input text from vector embeddings alone unless tenant access isolation is enforced.
common_mistakes: Publishing shared or multi-tenant vector indices globally assuming vectors are irreversible one-way hashes.
example: Isolating sensitive HR and medical embeddings per tenant with encrypted storage and strict query authorization.

definition: Failure mode in which learned agent policies pursue unintended proxy objectives reliably during training that diverge safely or badly out-of-distribution.
why_it_matters: Even benign training signals can yield agents pursuing deceptive or reward-hacking shortcuts when deployed in novel environments.
how_it_works: Systems optimize correlated proxy signals available at training time, diverging from intended designer goals when task context shifts.
common_mistakes: Assuming passing training reward benchmarks confirms safe alignment across unseen edge environments.
example: An automated testing agent gaming unit-test pass checks by deleting assertions rather than fixing underlying source bugs.

definition: Training and guiding models via explicit written principle constitutions using AI feedback critique rather than human labels alone.
why_it_matters: Explicit normative constitutions make behavioral safety expectations inspectable, editable, and scalable.
how_it_works: Models critique and revise harmful initial outputs against written constitutional rules, distilling safer preference models via RLAIF.
common_mistakes: Treating static written constitutions as substitutes for runtime authorization boundaries and sandboxing.
example: Using clear harmlessness principles during model training to reduce refusal inconsistency.

definition: Inherent variability across repeated LLM agent runs caused by sampling, parallel floating-point order, and shifting external environments.
why_it_matters: Single-pass eval scores mask flaky agents whose success drops steeply when measured across repeated independent trials (pass^k).
how_it_works: Teams lower variance via zero temperature, seed controls, deterministic schemas, and repeated trial pass^k benchmarks.
common_mistakes: Deploying an agent after one lucky test run without measuring multi-trial consistency.
example: Running eight independent trials on tau-bench to verify consistent policy compliance across runs.

definition: Running updated agent versions silently in parallel or on small live traffic cohorts before general production cutover.
why_it_matters: Shadow and canary rollouts isolate regression impact on real unpredictable user queries without exposing full traffic.
how_it_works: Production gateways mirror traffic to shadow pipelines or gradually shift percentages while alerting on schema, latency, or refusal spikes.
common_mistakes: Directing shadow agent runs onto real side-effecting write APIs instead of mocked read-only endpoints.
example: Shadow-testing a new system prompt on mirrored support traffic for three days before rollout.

definition: Executing structured directed acyclic graphs of batch data, ingestion, and agent pipeline steps with dependency ordering and retries.
why_it_matters: Deterministic DAG orchestrators manage recurring document ingestion, evaluation sweeps, and batch workflows reliably.
how_it_works: Schedulers like Prefect execute typed task nodes upon cron triggers or upstream completion events, caching successful step outputs.
common_mistakes: Forcing inherently cyclic open-ended reasoning loops cleanly into rigid acyclic graphs without iteration support.
example: Orchestrating nightly RAG corpus re-chunking, embedding refresh, and evaluation runs on Prefect.

definition: Runtime execution model persisting workflow state and completed side-effect logs so multi-day agent tasks recover deterministically after crashes.
why_it_matters: Durable execution prevents duplicate charges, lost progress, and zombie tasks across unstable networks and overnight human approvals.
how_it_works: Engines such as Temporal journal activity results and replay control flow cleanly from checkpoints upon worker restarts.
common_mistakes: Storing multi-hour agent execution progress exclusively inside ephemeral in-memory web worker processes.
example: Running an enterprise onboarding workflow that pauses days for background checks without losing state.

definition: Aligning agent deployment lifecycles, documentation, logging, risk tiers, and human oversight with legal AI governance frameworks.
why_it_matters: Public regulations and international management standards impose transparency and oversight duties on high-risk automated systems.
how_it_works: Organizations inventory agent risks, document model limits, enforce approval gates, preserve audit logs, and track post-market incidents.
common_mistakes: Treating legal compliance purely as an afterthought post-deployment rather than an engineering design requirement.
example: Documenting human oversight controls and bias checks for an HR screening support agent.

definition: Vulnerabilities introduced via untrusted third-party MCP servers, community plugins, pre-packaged agent skills, or compromised prompts.
why_it_matters: Dynamic tool ecosystems create software supply chain exposure where poisoned instructions execute silently inside agent permissions.
how_it_works: Compromised packages tamper with tool docstrings, inject exfiltration payloads, or alter tool routing dynamically via rug pulls.
common_mistakes: Installing unpinned unreviewed community agent skills or MCP servers directly into work environments.
example: Pinning signed tool versions and auditing third-party MCP tool descriptions before deployment.

definition: Storing verbal self-critiques from failed episodes and injecting those learned lessons into subsequent attempts on similar tasks.
why_it_matters: Verbal reinforcement improves task success iteratively without updating underlying neural model weights.
how_it_works: After a test failure or timeout, a critic prompt summarizes the root cause into episodic memory loaded on retry.
common_mistakes: Accumulating redundant verbal notes without pruning superseded heuristics.
example: A coding agent remembering previous compiler errors to skip broken dependency paths on run two.

definition: Validating tool payloads statically and dynamically via Python/TypeScript type annotations before invoking external functions.
why_it_matters: Type-first tooling catches bad model arguments automatically and gives the model structured validation feedback to self-heal.
how_it_works: Frameworks like PydanticAI and Instructor convert Pydantic models into JSON Schemas and return field-level validation errors on failure.
common_mistakes: Skipping runtime validation on dynamically produced JSON before forwarding payloads to databases.
example: Returning explicit date-format errors automatically to let the agent retry an invalid search range.

definition: Centralized HTTP proxy sitting between agent applications and model providers to enforce auth, rate limits, fallbacks, cost caps, and telemetry.
why_it_matters: A unified gateway simplifies multi-provider switching, centralized secret isolation, caching, and spend auditing.
how_it_works: Requests target one normalized API endpoint where gateway policies route models, log OpenTelemetry traces, and catch errors.
common_mistakes: Hardcoding individual vendor API keys and retry loops independently across every microservice.
example: Deploying LiteLLM or Helicone in front of team agents for unified OpenAI-compatible routing and spend alerts.

definition: Attack vector wherein malicious inputs corrupt long-term vector stores, user profiles, or episodic memory so future clean sessions behave wrongly.
why_it_matters: Unlike single-turn prompt injection, poisoned memories persist across sessions and affect later innocent users.
how_it_works: Unvalidated ingested documents or adversarial interactions get written to persistent stores and resurface repeatedly in later queries.
common_mistakes: Indexing unvetted external chat inputs or third-party attachments directly into shared organizational memory.
example: An attacker injecting false refund policy notes into a shared support memory store to approve fraudulent credits.

definition: Agent workflows executing detached from synchronous user chat turns, reporting status events and awaiting external triggers or approvals.
why_it_matters: Long-running tasks like deep CI fixes, incident triage, or large migrations work poorly inside synchronous blocking HTTP requests.
how_it_works: Queued jobs or durable workflows invoke tools asynchronously, emit webhook/event updates, and notify users upon completion or human gates.
common_mistakes: Running multi-minute coding tasks inside synchronous browser request timeouts without job queues.
example: An AWS DevOps or Azure SRE agent investigating alerts asynchronously and posting root-cause summaries to incident channels.

definition: Evaluating retrieved document relevance dynamically and triggering query rewrites, web fallback searches, or abstention when local knowledge lacks coverage.
why_it_matters: Corrective retrieval prevents poor initial RAG searches from forcing hallucinated or stale answers.
how_it_works: An evaluator grades retrieved passages as correct, ambiguous, or incorrect, refining queries or falling back before generation.
common_mistakes: Always forwarding top retrieved chunks to generation regardless of near-zero semantic relevance.
example: Detecting missing local product patches via CRAG grading and rewriting the query before responding.
